title: Numerical schemes
description: An Ornstein–Uhlenbeck drift with multiplicative noise, $dX^k_t = -X^k_t\,dt + \sigma\sqrt{1 + (X^k_t)^2}\,dW^k_t$ (Drift & noise window). The Δt sweep integrates many paths with every scheme at several step sizes, all driven by the same Brownian paths, and fits the convergence orders: the strong error $\mathbb{E}|X_T - X_T^{\mathrm{ref}}|$ and the weak error $|\mathbb{E}|X_T|^2 - \mathbb{E}|X_T^{\mathrm{ref}}|^2|$.

questions.text: Run the sweep. Strong order of Euler–Maruyama for this (multiplicative) noise?
Switch the state-dependent noise off (Drift & noise) and run the sweep again. Strong order of Euler–Maruyama now?
Why do Euler–Maruyama and Milstein give identical results for additive noise?
Strong or weak order: which one matters when you only want $\mathbb{E} f(X_T)$, and why can a scheme be good in one and poor in the other?
